cues.en: Bonjour mes dames et messieurs. Bonjour mes gouffers. Which if I translate... Of course, those who speak French understand that the translation of that is, hello, my waffles. I just learned that this weekend. Obviously, Go is successful. If you look at this room, look at what's going on here. And a lot of people have asked why Go is...
cues.zh: 女士们先生们，大家好。我的“华夫饼”们，大家好。要是翻译一下……当然，懂法语的人都知道，那句话的意思是：你好，我的华夫饼。我这也是这个周末才学到的。显而易见，Go 语言非常成功。看看这个房间，看看眼前的盛况。很多人都问过我为什么 Go 会如此……

cues.en: successful or I've asked me why Go is successful. And a lot of people have answers that involve tooling or the language or things about it. But I think those are all sort of superficial reasons. I think the real reason is simplicity. Go is simple, at least compared to a lot of other languages that are running around at the moment. But simplicity is actually a complicated subject and there are many ways to think about it.
cues.zh: 成功，或者问我 Go 成功的秘诀是什么。许多人的答案都离不开工具链、语言设计或者周边的特性。但我认为这些多少都有些浮于表面。我认为真正的核心是“简单”。Go 很简单，至少和目前活跃的许多其他语言相比是这样。但简单其实是个复杂的话题，有很多不同的思考角度。

cues.en: Last year, about May, I think, I went to a conference hosted by Microsoft called Langot Next. And I saw a number of actually quite interesting talks, many of which were the leaders of a particular language talking about a new version that was coming out, like JavaScript, PHP, C sharp, and so on. And I really was struck by one thing about these talks and these languages, which is most of the talks consisted of features being added by...
cues.zh: 去年大约五月的时候，我参加了微软主办的一个叫 Lang.NEXT 的大会。我听了一些相当有趣的演讲，其中不少是某门语言的带头人在介绍即将发布的新版本，比如 JavaScript、PHP、C# 等等。这些演讲和这些语言真正触动我的一点是，大部分演讲讲的都是如何通过……

cues.en: taking something from another language and adding it to this one. So, you know, JavaScript's getting classes and that kind of thing. And I realized that what's happening is all of these languages are turning into the same language. There's a concept called language relativity in linguistics, which is also colloquially called the Sapir-Worf hypothesis, although neither Sapir nor Worf quite agreed with it.
cues.zh: 从其他语言借鉴某个特性并加入到自己的语言中。比如，JavaScript 加入了 class 之类的特性。我意识到，照这样下去，所有这些语言都在慢慢趋同为同一种语言。语言学中有一个概念叫语言相对论，通俗点说就是“萨丕尔-沃尔夫假说”（Sapir-Whorf hypothesis），尽管萨丕尔和沃尔夫其实都算不上完全赞同它。

cues.en: And the idea is basically that language influences thought, and the sort of cartoon version is, you know, if you speak French, you're more amorous. And it's pretty obviously controversial. There's some evidence that there may be some truth, but not very much. But I think it's really obvious, if you think about it, that computer languages, this very much applies.
cues.zh: 它的核心观点基本上是说语言会影响思维，通俗的夸张说法就是：如果你说法语，你就会更多情浪漫。这显然是很有争议的。虽然有证据表明它可能有些道理，但并不充分。但如果你仔细琢磨一下，就会发现对于计算机语言来说，这个理论绝对非常适用。

cues.en: If you're in a logic programming language, you write a very different kind of program. You think a different way than if you're using an object-oriented programming language or a concurrent one. It's very much like disciplines in mathematics. You don't solve calculus using linear algebra, even though they have some structural comparisons. And so I'm worried about this trend in the languages, because they all converge to the same language. We're all going to be thinking the same way. And that would make life very, very uninteresting.
cues.zh: 如果你用的是逻辑编程语言，你写出来的程序会截然不同。你的思考方式也会完全不同于使用面向对象语言或并发编程语言时的思考方式。这很像数学中的不同学科。你不会用线性代数去解微积分，尽管它们在结构上有某些相似之处。所以我对语言的这种发展趋势感到担忧，因为如果它们全都趋同为同一种语言，我们所有人的思考方式都会变得千篇一律。那生活可就太无趣了。

cues.en: You want to have different languages for different problems. You want to have different domains be solved by different ways of thinking and different notations. In other words, you kind of want a tool that's optimized for each particular way you're working. Now, these talks at Lang.next were about things like Java 8, ECMAScript 6, which has been a long time coming, C Sharp, C++ 14, and there are a few others that didn't quite fit this mold, but let's just talk about the ones that do. As I said, these languages are evolving by adding features.
cues.zh: 你希望用不同的语言解决不同的问题。希望不同的领域能用不同的思维方式和符号体系来解决。换句话说，你希望每个具体的工作方式都能有量身定制的工具。这次在 Lang.next 上的演讲，讲的大多是 Java 8、让人翘首以盼的 ECMAScript 6、C Sharp、C++ 14 之类的东西，还有少数几个不太符合这种模式，但我们只聊符合的。正如我所说，这些语言都是通过不断添加特性来演进的。

cues.en: That means they're becoming more complicated. Their complexity is growing while they are simultaneously becoming more similar to one another. That's a very strange situation for a field to be in. I would summarize that as bloat without distinction. Go, however, as I hope you appreciate, isn't like that. Go is a different language in this respect. It doesn't try to be like these other languages because it's not taking features.
cues.zh: 这意味着它们变得越来越复杂。它们的复杂度在增长，同时彼此之间却越来越相似。这对一个领域来说是种非常奇怪的境况。我会把它总结为“毫无特色的臃肿”。然而，正如我希望大家能体会到的，Go 并不是这样。在这方面，Go 是一门不同的语言。它并不想变得和其它语言一样，因为它没有盲目堆砌特性。

cues.en: It doesn't try to compete by saying, oh, if they have that feature, we better have it, or people will be unwilling to use their language. In fact, as of Go 1, which is, what, three years old now? The language is fixed. You may have noticed that the features that have gone in since then are absolutely tiny. There's really been no significant change to the language since Go 1, and that was the point of Go 1. However, many newcomers to Go start by asking,
cues.zh: 它不会为了竞争而觉得：哎呀，他们有那个特性，我们最好也加上，不然大家就不愿意用我们的语言了。实际上，从 Go 1 开始——大概已经是三年前了吧？这门语言就定型了。你可能已经注意到，从那之后加入的特性微乎其微。自 Go 1 以来，这门语言确实没有任何重大改动，而这正是 Go 1 的初衷。然而，很多 Go 的新手一上来就会问：

cues.en: Can we add this feature to the language? Can we make error handling different? Can we change the way arrays work or something like that? But the language is fixed. Those things don't get to go in. But it's not just that the language is fixed. It's because adding features will not really make Go better. And why is that true? It would just make it bigger, but it would make it less different. And both of those are worse, in my opinion. But obviously, you need features. You can't have a programming language without some features in it.
cues.zh: “我们能不能给语言加上这个特性？能不能改改错误处理机制？能不能改一下数组的工作方式？”诸如此类。但语言已经定型了。这些东西加不进来。但这不仅仅是因为语言定型了，更是因为增加特性并不会让 Go 真正变好。为什么这么说呢？这只会让它变得更庞大，同时失去独特性。在我看来，这两点都是倒退。不过显然，特性是必需的。一门编程语言不可能没有任何特性。

cues.en: But which ones? Well, obviously the right ones. And so we picked the right ones. How did we pick the right ones? Well, one way is that the original language was designed by Ken Thompson, Robert Griesemer, and myself. And we all have very different backgrounds. Ken and I had worked together at Bell Labs quite a bit, but we also had done very different things, and Ken is a god. So when we came to talk about what was going into the language, we insisted that all three of us not only agreed with the feature going in, but agreed that it was the right feature to go in.
cues.zh: 但该选哪些？显然要选正确的特性。所以我们挑选了正确的那些。我们是怎么挑出来的？一方面，最初这门语言是由 Ken Thompson、Robert Griesemer 和我共同设计的。我们的背景截然不同。我和 Ken 曾在 Bell Labs 共事良久，但做过的事情也大相径庭，而且 Ken 是个神级人物。所以每当我们讨论要把什么加入语言时，我们都坚持：必须三个人不仅都同意加这个特性，还要一致认同它就是那个该加的正确特性。

cues.en: And with our different backgrounds and our different perspectives, that dramatically narrowed the number of things that went into Go. But you still have to pick what to put in. And our overriding thing for doing this was readability. And here's how we think about this. If a language has too many features, or even more than you might need, you spend time programming thinking about which features to use.
cues.zh: 正因为我们有着不同的背景和视角，进入 Go 的特性数量被大幅缩减。但你依然得决定放什么进去，而我们做这件事的首要准则就是可读性。我们是这么想的：如果一门语言有太多特性，甚至多于你实际所需的，你写代码时就会分心去琢磨该用哪些特性。

cues.en: If there's really a lot of features, you may look at the line of code, write it one way. Ooh, I could do something different. I could use this feature, I could use that feature. You might even spend half an hour playing with a few lines of code to find all the right ways you could use different features to make the code work a certain way. And it's kind of a waste of time to do that. But worse, when you come back to the program later, you have to recreate that thought process. You not only have to understand this complicated program,
cues.zh: 如果特性真的很多，你看着一行代码，这样写出来了，接着又想：哎，我还可以换种写法，我可以用这个特性，也可以用那个特性。你甚至可能花半小时折腾这几行代码，尝试各种特性组合来达到某种效果。这么做纯属浪费时间。但更糟的是，日后当你重新回来看这段程序时，你必须重建当年的思考过程。你不仅要理解这个复杂的程序、

cues.en: programming language doing whatever it's doing, you have to understand why the programmer who might be you decided that this was the way to approach the problem from the feature set available. And that is just, I think, bad engineering. The summarization of this is the code is harder to understand simply because it is using a more complex language. You want to have just one way or at least fewer simpler, easier to understand ways. So in other words, features add complexity.
cues.zh: 理解编程语言底层在干什么，还得去琢磨写代码的人（可能就是你自己）为什么从一堆可用特性中挑了这种解法。我认为这完全是糟糕的工程实践。简而言之，代码更难懂仅仅是因为它使用了一种更复杂的语言。你希望只有一种写法，或者至少是更少、更简单、更容易理解的写法。换句话说，特性会增加复杂度。

cues.en: We want simplicity. Features hurt readability. We really want readability. And readability is, by my opinion, the most important feature of a programming language. Because readable means reliable. If you can read the code and know what it means, then it's easier to understand. It's easier to work on. It's easier to extend. It's easier to fix when it breaks. It's easier to understand why it's broken. These are all good things. And that is why readability is so important. If the language is complicated, on the other hand,
cues.zh: 我们追求的是简单。特性会伤害可读性，而我们极其看重可读性。在我看来，可读性是一门编程语言最重要的特性。因为可读意味着可靠。如果你能读懂代码并清楚它的含义，它就更容易理解。更容易修改、更容易扩展、出故障时更容易修复，也更容易排查坏掉的原因。这些全都是好处。这就是为什么可读性如此重要。反过来说，如果语言很复杂，

cues.en: You have to understand more to understand even where to start working on the program. And you have to understand a more complicated model in which the program is being written. These cost time and make the language harder to use. But there's a tradeoff. Obviously, making more features in a language gives you more fun things to play with. And so there's a fundamental tradeoff in Go that was made in a different direction from most other languages. And the tradeoff is, what do you want? A language that's more fun to write in?
cues.zh: 你甚至得先理解更多东西才知道从何下手。你还必须理解编写该程序所依赖的更复杂的模型。这些都会消耗时间，让语言更难用。但这需要权衡。显然，语言特性越多，玩起来的花样就越多。因此 Go 做出了一个根本性的权衡，选择了一条与其他大多数语言不同的道路。这个权衡就是：你究竟想要什么？是一门写起来更有趣的语言？

cues.en: or easier to work on and maintain. And for the most part, the decisions in Go about what went in were about long-term maintenance, and particularly in the context of large-scale programming, although that's a little off the topic today. Now, the thing is, you put features in to make languages expressive. You obviously want to not have to type hexadecimal numbers, which would be a very low-feature way to write code, but obviously very hard to use. But you have to be careful, because if you make something too concise, it can become...
cues.zh: 还是一门更容易上手和维护的语言？在很大程度上，Go 决定加入什么特性，主要考虑的都是长期维护，尤其是在大规模编程的场景下——虽然这有点偏离今天的主题了。问题的核心在于，加入特性是为了提升语言的表达能力。你肯定不想去敲十六进制数字，那种写代码的方式特性极少，但显然极难使用。不过你必须小心，因为如果你把东西做得太简洁，它就可能会变成……

cues.en: just unreadable. This example here is a real working program in a dialect of APL called Dialog, and it implements Conway's Game of Life. And I think you could argue that even if you're an expert APL programmer, it's not very readable. APL is famous for being easy to write and hard to read. And I think we have to be very careful we don't write software like this in a modern, distributed, multi-programmer, open source world. But there's a more important point, I think, well, maybe an equally important point.
cues.zh: 简直读不懂。这里展示的是一个真正可运行的程序，用的是 APL 的一种方言 Dyalog，实现了康威生命游戏。我觉得即便是 APL 专家，也会承认这代码可读性很差。APL 向来以“好写难读”著称。我认为在如今这个分布式、多人协作、开源的世界里，我们必须非常小心，绝不能写出这样的软件。不过我觉得还有一个更重要、或者说同样重要的点。

cues.en: which is when you have features that add expressiveness, they typically add expense. For instance, a lot of people have asked for things like map and filter to be built into Go, and we've said no. One of the reasons we've said no is that if you have things like map and filter, they're going to use them. That's why they're there. But they may be more expensive than a simple for loop. And when the features are there to make life easier and more expressive, they tend to generate more...
cues.zh: 那就是：当你引入增加表达力的特性时，通常也会增加开销。比如很多人曾要求在 Go 中内置像 map 和 filter 这样的功能，但我们拒绝了。拒绝的原因之一是，如果你提供了 map 和 filter，大家就会去用，毕竟它们就是为此而生的。但它们的开销可能远比一个简单的 for 循环大得多。而当这些特性为了让开发更轻松、更具表现力而存在时，往往会产生更……

cues.en: expensive in terms of computer time solutions to problems that have much simpler solutions. So they may help the programmer, although not always, but they'll almost always hurt the computer unless the implementation is extremely smart. And believe me, the implementation of APL is extremely smart. So that actually is a modestly efficient implementation of the game of life. But you could do much, much better if you wrote a simpler program. But you've got to be careful, because if you make everything too expensive and explain everything in detail, you get a very verbose language.
cues.zh: ……在机器耗时上更昂贵的解法，而这些问题明明有简单得多的方案。所以它们或许能帮到程序员（也并不总是如此），但几乎总是在折磨计算机，除非底层实现极其聪明。相信我，APL 的实现确实极其聪明，所以那段生命游戏的代码其实效率还算过得去。但如果写一个更朴素的程序，性能可以好得多。不过你也得注意，如果所有东西都太笨重、把每件事都事无巨细地交待一遍，语言就会变得极其啰唆。

cues.en: I won't name any, but you know the ones I'm thinking of, where it just seems like you're writing too much to say a simple thing. So you have to balance this. So what we did was we tried to make the right selection, building on the ideas that were familiar so that a programmer with a background in procedural programming, like with C or Java or even Fortran, say, could read a Go program and get a pretty good idea right out of the box what was happening and not be confused by strange notation.
cues.zh: 我就不点名了，但你们知道我想的是哪些语言——表达一件简单的事却要写一大堆代码。所以你必须做权衡。我们的做法是尽量做出恰当的选择，基于大家熟悉的理念来构建，让具有过程式编程背景的开发者（比如熟悉 C、Java 甚至 Fortran 的人）在看一段 Go 程序时，上手就能大致看懂它在做什么，而不会被奇怪的符号搞糊涂。

cues.en: So you have to balance. You have to be concise, but be expressive. Make sure that the program's easy to read. You have to pick the right set of features, in other words. Not just features for feature's sake. The way I like to think of this is to think of the entire world of programming as a vector space of very high dimension. And what you want to do is to find the basis set that covers that vector space so that you can write the programs you want by combining the appropriate orthogonal
cues.zh: 所以你必须权衡。既要简洁，又要富有表现力，同时确保程序易读。换句话说，你必须精选一套合适的特性，而不是为了加特性而加特性。我喜欢把整个编程世界想象成一个超高维度的向量空间。而你要做的，是找到覆盖这个向量空间的一组基底，这样你就可以通过组合恰当的正交……

cues.en: because that's what basis it is, orthogonal set of features. And what happens when you add features for expressiveness or for fun is it tends to add more non-basis vectors into that space, and so there become many paths to get to a particular solution. So that's when we say features are orthogonal, that's what we mean. We mean that they cover this space, but we also mean they interact really well. So if you take feature A and feature B and you write a program that uses them, they work exactly the way you expect feature A and feature B to work.
cues.zh: ……正交特性集，因为基底的本质就是正交的。而当你单纯为了表达力或觉得好玩而添加特性时，往往会向这个空间塞入更多非基底向量，导致实现同一个解法的路径变得过多。所以当我们说特性是“正交”的时候，指的就是这个意思。既指它们能覆盖这个空间，也指它们能很好地协同工作。如果把特性 A 和特性 B 组合起来写程序，它们的表现就会完全符合你对特性 A 和特性 B 各自的预期。

cues.en: They're not in some weird diagonal that causes all kinds of complications you have to worry about. Again, I won't mention which language I'm thinking of. So you have to keep all of this in mind when you're designing a language, and also think about what the goal is. What are you actually trying to achieve? What is the problem domain that this language is being done for? Well, in Go's case, we were trying to write code for Google, because that's what we do. In Go's software, the parts that we worked on are mostly infrastructure, server infrastructure, what we now call cloud software, but used to just be called servers.
cues.zh: 它们不在某种奇怪的对角线上，不会引起各种你必须担心的复杂问题。再说一遍，我不会提我想到的是哪门语言。所以设计语言时你得记住所有这些，还要想想目标是什么。你实际想达成什么？这门语言是为哪个问题域而做的？在 Go 的情况下，我们是想为 Google 写代码，因为这就是我们做的事。在 Go 软件里，我们参与的部分主要是基础设施、服务器基础设施，现在叫云软件，但过去就叫服务器。

cues.en: And to do this, you have to find enough pieces to build the software. And so the fundamental components we started with were ideas like concrete data types, you know, integers, structures, floating point numbers, functions and methods, interfaces, packages, concurrency, and then the sort of guiding engineering principle of having a really good fast implementation with the ability to have really good tooling. And with all those guidelines, which is a fairly complicated set of considerations,
cues.zh: 要做到这一点，你得找到足够多的构件来构建软件。所以我们起步时的基本组件是具体数据类型，比如整数、结构体、浮点数、函数和方法、接口、包、并发，然后是一个指导性工程原则：要有非常好的快速实现，同时能提供非常好的工具。带着所有这些准则——这是一套相当复杂的考量——

cues.en: the pieces sort of fell into place, and actually ended up being kind of simple in practice. And in fact, simplicity can be expressive. This is a very simple drawing. René drew this a while back, and yet he's expressive, right? He's not really a gopher, and I'm not talking about the Magritte version of Sesina Bazungoufer. I mean, he's just the representation of a gopher, very much like Shreve's talk earlier with the horse, right? And so this for me is what...
cues.zh: 这些部分就各就各位了，实际做出来还挺简单。事实上，简单也可以有表现力。这是一幅非常简单的画。René 前阵子画的，可它很有表现力，对吧？它并不是真的地鼠，我也不是在说 Magritte 版的 Sesina Bazungoufer。我是说，它只是地鼠的表示，很像 Shreve 早些时候演讲里那匹马，对吧？所以对我来说，这就是……

cues.en: is part of like the ethos of Go. Here's this really simple drawing that represents what Go is like. We could put more features on it. We could make it more like a gopher. We could give them lots more detail. And we get something like this, right? But mostly what we've added is ugliness and hair. We haven't actually made him better. It's complexity without clarity. But I want to make a really important point here, which is I've said Go is simple, but it's not. It's very complicated. I know. I worked on it. It's one of the most complicated things I've ever worked on.
cues.zh: 是 Go 精神气质的一部分。这是一幅非常简单的画，代表了 Go 是什么样。我们可以给它加更多特性。我们可以让它更像地鼠。我们可以给它加更多细节。然后得到这样的东西，对吧？但我们加上的主要是丑陋和毛发。我们其实没让它更好。这是没有清晰度的复杂度。但这里我想强调一个非常重要的点：我说过 Go 很简单，但它不是。它非常复杂。我知道。我参与过。它是我做过的最复杂的东西之一。

cues.en: And yet it feels simple. And I think that's a really important idea. And it feels simple because these pieces fit together orthogonally. And that requires a lot of design, a lot of thinking, a lot of refinement and implementation and re-implementation. And to put it very bluntly, simplicity, at least in this context, is the art of hiding complexity. So let me talk about a few simple things in Go and why they're really complicated. Garbage collection, Go routines, constants, interface, and packages.
cues.zh: 但它感觉很简单。我觉得这是个非常重要的理念。它之所以感觉简单，是因为这些部分正交地契合在一起。而这需要大量设计、大量思考、大量细化和实现、再实现。说得直白些，简单——至少在这个语境下——是隐藏复杂度的艺术。那我来谈谈 Go 里几个简单的东西，以及它们为什么其实很复杂。垃圾回收、goroutine、常量、接口和包。

cues.en: Each of these things is very simple and very complicated, but at the same time, there's a lot of other subjects I could pick, but let's quickly go through these. Garbage collection's probably the best example of simplicity hiding complexity. What is the programmer interface for garbage collection? There isn't one. Can't get simpler than that. The empty set is as simple as it gets, right? And yet, look how hard it is to implement.
cues.zh: 这些东西每一样都既非常简单又非常复杂，但同时我还可以挑很多其他主题，不过我们先快速过一遍这些。垃圾回收可能是“简单掩盖复杂”的最佳例子。程序员使用垃圾回收的接口是什么？根本没有。没有比这更简单的了。空集就是最简单的，对吧？可你看看实现起来有多难。

cues.en: all that incredible code to deal with stack maps and copying the stacks when you need to grow them and tracking all the references down, pausing it, running in parallel with the mutator. It's a tremendously complicated problem that fortunately I didn't have to work on. We have some really good people in the Go team who did. But I think it's amazing to consider how much code is there for something that has absolutely no user interface. There isn't even a free function in Go. There's nothing but garbage collection to manage memory.
cues.zh: 要处理栈映射、在栈需要增长时复制栈、追踪所有引用、暂停程序、与 mutator 并行运行，所有这些了不起的代码。这是一个极其复杂的问题，幸运的是我不用去做。Go 团队里有一些非常优秀的人做了这件事。但想想看，一个完全没有用户界面的东西却有那么多的代码，真令人惊叹。Go 里甚至连 free 函数都没有。管理内存除了垃圾回收，什么都没有。

cues.en: And it's remarkable to point out that it isn't even in the spec. The goal language does not define it. It is garbage collected in the specification. The only mention is in the introduction was a throwaway property of a feature of the language. That's how small and therefore how simple the spec is. I mean, the garbage collection is. And yet how complicated it is behind the scenes. And it also makes code simpler because you don't have to think about who owns the data, who's going to free it, how to manage it for you. You can...
cues.zh: 值得注意的是，它甚至不在规范里。Go 语言并没有定义它。规范里只说它会被垃圾回收。唯一提到它的地方是在引言里，作为语言某个特性的附带属性。规范就是这么小，因此也这么简单。我是说，垃圾回收这部分。可它在幕后有多复杂。而且它也让代码更简单，因为你不用考虑谁拥有数据、谁来释放、怎么替你管理。你可以……

cues.en: Think about implementation details and efficiency, but for just straightforward Go programming, garbage collection hides everything. It's fantastic. One of the things that people love about Go is the concurrency. I think it's arguably one of the simplest concurrency models available in a programming language. Not that there are that many, but there are some others. There's several components to it. Go routines, channels, and select. And I'm going to talk about Go routines for a minute. You start a Go routine with the Go keyword. You say Go space, Go space, and then a function call.
cues.zh: 你可以考虑实现细节和效率，但对于普通的 Go 编程，垃圾回收把这一切都隐藏起来。太棒了。人们喜欢 Go 的一点是并发。我认为它可以说是编程语言中最简单的并发模型之一。倒不是说这样的模型很多，但也确实有一些别的。它有几个组成部分：goroutine、channel 和 select。我要花一分钟讲讲 goroutine。你用 go 关键字启动一个 goroutine。你输入 go 加空格，go 加空格，然后是一个函数调用。

cues.en: So three keystrokes. You can't make it much shorter than that. I can imagine one or two changes I could make. But three keystrokes, and you've just started a subprocess in the general mathematical term. And so it's like garbage collection, because it's extremely simple UI. There's nothing in the UI about the size of the stack, or a thread ID, or managing go routines, trim down, things like that. There's no completion status. There's no type.
cues.zh: 所以是三次按键。你没法让它更短了。我能想到可以做一两处改动。但敲三下，你就启动了一个子进程——按一般术语来说。所以它就像垃圾回收，因为界面极其简单。界面里没有栈大小、线程 ID，也没有管理 goroutine、缩减、销毁之类的东西。没有完成状态，也没有类型。

cues.en: A lot of people ask for these things, and in fact, some other languages or thread packages provide the equivalent functionality of some of those things, but we didn't put them in. We wanted to go keyword to be so simple that it had the minimum possible UI. Here's a function call, run it alongside my other things, three keystrokes. And that's part of this minimal design. And in Khrushchev's talk earlier today, he talked about one of the reasons I think you can appreciate now, why, for instance, there's no ID on a Go routine.
cues.zh: 很多人要求这些功能，实际上，其他一些语言或线程包也提供了其中某些功能的等价物，但我们没有把它们放进去。我们希望 go 关键字尽可能简单，拥有最小可能的 UI。这里有一个函数调用，让它和我的其他东西一起跑，三次按键。这是极简设计的一部分。在今天早些时候 Khrushchev 的演讲中，他谈到了一个原因——我想你现在能理解了——比如为什么 goroutine 没有 ID。

cues.en: Internally, of course, you have a lot of complexity managing this, managing the relationship between the Go routine implementation, the runtime stack, and the garbage collector, for example. Incredibly complicated behind-the-scenes stuff. But three keystrokes. Constants. This is one of my favorite things about Go that most people don't even think about. And they don't think about it because it's incredibly simple. When we decided that Go had to be strictly tight,
cues.zh: 当然，内部要管理这些，要管理 goroutine 实现、运行时栈和垃圾回收器之间的关系等等，复杂度很高。幕后东西极其复杂。但只是三次按键。常量。这是我最喜欢的 Go 特性之一，大多数人甚至不会去想它。他们不去想，是因为它极其简单。当我们决定 Go 必须严格类型时，

cues.en: That meant that numeric types could not be interchanged freely. That was a very common source of bugs in C and C++. You were not allowed in Go to take an int and put it into a float64 or anything like that. But that can be very clumsy. You don't want to have to say float64 zero every time you want to use a floating point zero. So we had this idea, which is one of Go's, I think, relatively novel ideas, which is that we made constants just be numbers. They're just numbers.
cues.zh: 这意味着数值类型不能自由互换。这是 C 和 C++ 中非常常见的 bug 来源。在 Go 里，你不能拿一个 int 放进 float64 之类的东西里。但那会非常笨拙。你不会想每次要用浮点零时都得写 float64(0)。所以我们有了这个想法，我认为这是 Go 相对新颖的想法之一：我们让常量就只是数字。它们就只是数字。

cues.en: even though the language is strictly tight. And this means you get to throw around things like one e nine dividing into a time dot second, which has a strict type. And to get this to work was really hard. It was one of the hardest things in designing language, not in implementing it so much, but designing it. We had to worry about what infinite precision integers mean, what infinite precision floating point means, what happens to the promotion rules if you divide an integer two versus divide a floating point two.
cues.zh: 尽管这门语言是严格类型的。这意味着你可以随手写 1e9 除以 time.Second 这样的东西，而 time.Second 是有严格类型的。要让这工作起来真的很难。这是设计语言时最难的事情之一，与其说实现难，不如说设计难。我们得操心无限精度整数意味着什么、无限精度浮点数意味着什么，以及把整数 2 相除和把浮点 2 相除时，类型提升规则会发生什么。

cues.en: And you get corner cases like this crazy shift, which I can't run, but what do you think the answer is to this? What does this program print? It's got a 2.0 and a 2.0 shift at zero, and asking the type of both of them. You have to think, don't you? This is a place where the complexity comes out. You actually get a float, 64, and an int. And that's not a good thing. It's just the consequence of the rules that we eventually converged on to make constants work right.
cues.zh: 然后你会遇到这种疯狂移位之类的边界情况，我跑不了它，但你觉得答案是什么？这个程序会打印什么？它有一个 2.0 和一个 2.0 移位 0，然后问两者的类型。你得想一想，对吧？这就是复杂性冒出来的地方。你实际得到一个 float64 和一个 int。这不是什么好事。它只是我们最终为了让常量正确工作而收敛到的那套规则的结果。

cues.en: But for the most part, you never see these kind of words when you're using constants. They just feel like numbers, and it's fantastic. So I'm not totally satisfied, but I think it was a really good example, again, of simplicity hiding complexity. And I wrote a blog post on blog.goaling.org slash constants that talks about this stuff in much more detail. Interfaces, one of Go's favorite features for myself and I think for a lot of Go programmers, a very simple idea. All there is is a set of methods.
cues.zh: 但大多数时候，你用常量时根本看不到这类词。它们感觉就像数字，这太棒了。所以我并不完全满意，但我认为这又是一个很好的例子：简单隐藏复杂性。我在 blog.golang.org/constants 写了一篇博客文章，更详细地讨论了这些东西。接口，这是我自己最喜欢的 Go 特性之一，我想对很多 Go 程序员也是如此，一个非常简单的想法。它全部内容就是一组方法。

cues.en: People ask for data as well all the time. Not going to get it. It's just functions. Very simple. You also need a variable of type interface so you can program with these things. But even here, you get some funny things happening. Because you, for instance, can assign OS dot std into a reader. No problem. You can assign OS dot std into an empty interface. No problem. But if you have to narrow the interface, you have to do a dynamic type check, which we call the type assertion.
cues.zh: 人们也总想要数据。但根本拿不到。就只有函数。非常简单。你还需要一个接口类型的变量，才能用这些东西来编程。但即便在这里，也会发生一些有趣的事。比如，你可以把 os.Stdin 赋给 Reader。没问题。你可以把 os.Stdin 赋给空接口。也没问题。但如果要收窄接口范围，就必须做动态类型检查，也就是我们说的类型断言。

cues.en: And one of the things that's not well-known about Go is that was not in the original design. We realized a few months into it that we needed type assertions to make the program work right. The addition of effectively dynamic typing into a statically programmed language was a complicated thing that we had to deal with and make it work. And I'm not totally thrilled with how it worked out, but I think it's pretty good. And it does, in the end, do its job. But for the most part, what you have again is a very simple idea that interfaces a set of methods.
cues.zh: 关于 Go，鲜为人知的一点是它原本并不在最初的设计中。写了几个月后，我们才意识到需要类型断言才能让程序正常工作。在一个静态语言中引入实质上的动态类型，是一件非常棘手的事情，我们必须解决并让它跑通。虽然我对最终的实现并不算完全满意，但我认为已经很不错了。归根结底，它确实发挥了作用。但大部分情况下，核心理念依然非常简单：接口就是一组方法。

cues.en: And with, again, a quite complicated set of rules behind them that mostly just do what you want. But it was hard. In fact, interfaces are probably Go's most distinctive and powerful feature. I think concurrency is talked about a little more. But you don't write as much concurrency in a typical program as you use interfaces. Interfaces have a profound effect on the library. They've enabled the very structure of Go programs to be the way they are with, I think, the most component-oriented architecture of any programming language I've used. And so they, in fact,
cues.zh: 同样，它背后有一套相当复杂的规则，大多时候都能顺从你的意图。但做起来很难。事实上，接口可能是 Go 最独特、最强大的特性。我想大家平时讨论并发会更多一些。但在典型程序中，写并发代码的频率远不如用接口高。接口对标准库产生了深远的影响。它们塑造了 Go 现有的程序结构，在用过的所有编程语言中，我认为它提供了最契合组件化导向的架构。所以事实上，

cues.en: I think can safely say they are simple to use, even though they add complexity, they're worth it. And finally, packages. Packages are one of the hardest things we had to deal with in designing a language. It doesn't seem like there's anything there. What do you have? Do you have package big? There's the name of the package. You have an import string in the client. What's there? It took us months to figure this out, because it interacts with things like scoping, naming,
cues.zh: 我想完全可以说它们用起来很简单，即使增加了复杂性，也是值得的。最后是包（package）。包是我们在语言设计中遇到的最棘手的问题之一。表面上看似乎平平无奇。能有什么呢？写个 package big？这就是包名了。调用方那里有个 import 字符串。还能有什么？我们花了几个月才搞明白，因为它牵涉到作用域、命名、

cues.en: information hiding, isolation, linking, compiling, cross-compiling, and getting all those details right took a very, very long time. But on the other hand, you guys never think about this stuff, right? They just work. Somebody earlier today said import was his favorite keyword. That's great. I love it.
cues.zh: 信息隐藏、隔离、链接、编译、交叉编译等方方面面，要把所有细节都做对，花了非常非常长的时间。但从另一个角度看，大家平时根本不用操心这些，对吧？它开箱即用。今天早些时候有人说 import 是他最喜欢的关键字。太棒了，我很喜欢。

cues.en: And all that complexity, which is fantastically intricate when you start talking about working across multiple implementations for different architectures and different operating systems, it's all hidden behind this simple package idea that has basically two concepts. And that includes the things like go get, which is a fantastic enabler for open source based on the fact that the import string is literally that, a string with no semantic meaning within the language. So again,
cues.zh: 所有那些复杂性——特别是当你面对不同架构和不同操作系统的多套实现时，极其繁琐——全都被隐藏在了包这个极其简单的概念背后，它基本上就两个核心要素。这也催生了像 go get 这样的利器，它极大地推动了开源，这完全建立在 import 字符串就仅仅是一个字符串的事实上，在语言内部没有任何语义。所以再次强调，

cues.en: Very hard to implement, very complicated under the covers, extremely simple to use. And I think after garbage collection, packages are actually the best example of simplicity hiding complexity. Let me show you. Here's a simple example. It's just the sort of standard Hello World server. It's written with some Japanese in it, because why not? But you all, I think, can recognize as competent Go programmers very quickly what that program does. I don't need to run it. It does run. It does what you think.
cues.zh: 实现起来极难，底层极其复杂，用起来却无比简单。我认为在垃圾回收之后，包其实是“以简洁隐藏复杂”的最佳范例。我来演示一下。这里有个简单的例子。就是一个标准的 Hello World 服务器。里面混写了点日文，图个乐子。但我想在座合格的 Go 开发者，都能一眼看出这个程序是干什么的。我就不运行了。它确实能跑，而且效果完全如你所料。

cues.en: Very simple, right? There's hardly anything there. Just a few lines of code, starts a server, runs it. OK, here's what's going on inside this program. First of all, most visibly, it's doing Unicode and UTF-8, working flawlessly. It's importing some magic packages, and they're being used. Func, log, net, HTTP, and HTTP being one of the most awesome packages. There's an F per def directly to a network connection, which is interesting and unusual.
cues.zh: 很简单，对吧？几乎没写什么。就几行代码，启动服务器并运行。好，看看这个程序内部发生了什么。首先最明显的是，它在处理 Unicode 和 UTF-8，而且完美无瑕。它导入了一些神奇的包，并且确实用到了。Func、log、net、HTTP，其中 HTTP 是最棒的包之一。有一个 func 直接挂到网络连接上，这很有意思，也不寻常。

cues.en: There's a function being promoted to a method with the handle func in there, which is a bit of a mind blow to people new to go. It was mind blow to me when it was pointed out to me by Russ that we could do that. It's also truly concurrent. The server won't block. As long as there's enough resources on the server hardware, you can have zillions of people talking to this service simultaneously, which is to say it's production ready. There it is, a production ready web server in just a few lines of code. It doesn't get much simpler than that, right?
cues.zh: 有一个函数通过里面的 handle func 被提升为方法，这对刚接触 Go 的人来说有点颠覆认知。当 Russ 指出我们可以这么做时，我也被震撼到了。它还是真正并发的。服务器不会阻塞。只要服务器硬件资源足够，就能让无数人同时访问这个服务，也就是说它已经生产可用。看，一个生产可用的 Web 服务器，只用了短短几行代码。再简单不过了，对吧？

cues.en: So, in summary, simplicity is complicated, but the clarity is worth the fight. I don't want to hang out with the gopher on the right. I want to hang out with the guy on the left. He's much more expressive and fun and much less hairy. So, in conclusion, simplicity is very hard to design. It's very complicated to build. It sounds strange to say that, but it's true. Making things simple is hard work. But if you get it right...
cues.zh: 所以总结一下，简单这件事本身很复杂，但清晰值得去争取。我不想和右边那只 gopher 一起玩，我想和左边这位一起玩。他更有表现力、更有趣，也没那么多毛。所以结论是，简单非常难设计，构建起来也非常复杂。这么说听起来奇怪，但确实如此。把东西做简单是苦功夫。但如果你做对了……

cues.en: you get something that's very easy to use. And I think the success of Go and the fact that you're all here listening to me proves that there's something there. Thank you.
cues.zh: 你就能得到非常易用的东西。我认为 Go 的成功，以及你们都在这里听我讲，证明了它确实有可取之处。谢谢。
